_comment: What grows in the Meadows playground, and where. ALL of it is TUNABLE. The expected feedback is 'too sparse', 'too busy', 'the trees are on the cliffs' — every one of those has to be answerable here rather than in a scene.
_comment_authored: This dresses the M1 MOVEMENT PLAYGROUND, not the real Meadows. M7 authors the actual geography and its placement will be authored rather than scattered. The RULES survive that; the specific clump centres do not.
_comment_clumping: Every layer clusters. Evenly-spread props at uniform scale are the readable signature of generator output — the visual rubric names it — so each layer places clumps and scatters within them, leaving clearings between. `strays` fills the gaps so the clumps do not read as islands.
_comment_pack: Quaternius Stylized Nature MegaKit (CC0), replacing Kenney's Nature Kit. The blind critic's verdict on the Kenney set was that every tree was the same tree — 'one straight tapered trunk, one 6-8 face canopy, two greens, varied only by uniform scale' — and that the far tree line read as 'a row of identical cards at near-uniform spacing along a contour: a fence of icons'. It measured mid-distance trees at 1.00:1 luminance contrast against the ground behind them, meaning invisible. This pack ships four genuinely different tree species with real bark and leaf TEXTURES and normal maps, which is what that complaint was actually about.
_comment_scale: These models are authored in METRES, unlike Kenney's which were about one unit tall and needed a 3.4x per-layer correction. So `base_scale` is near 1.0 here and mostly trims rather than multiplies. Measured with tools/measure_models.gd rather than guessed — guessing produced a meadow of knee-high trees once already.
_comment_ev2: EV2 (bible sec10): an APPROVED SUBSET, not all 116 models in the fuller pack. `trees` (standard canopy) and `grove` (hero trees) are each cut to the bible's counts and given controlled spring/deep/yellow-green variants per model instead of one flat colour; `saplings` is new. Two of the bible's asks are NOT done here and are recorded rather than faked: 'wetland forms near river' was blocked on there being no water at all; EV5 has since shipped the pond/stream and reed stands at the banks, but a dedicated wetland MESH still does not exist; and the rock family's '2-3 large' tier has no distinct large-format mesh in the imported subset (the fuller Stylized Nature MegaKit is itch.io-blocked, see EV1-remainder in BLOCKED.md) — reusing the existing Rock_Medium meshes in a second layer would silently break their tint/collision via vegetation.gd's known models-shared-across-layers failure mode, so the existing single `rocks` layer's 0.28-2.1 scale span (already producing large-boulder reads from the same 3 medium meshes) stands as the honest ceiling until more geometry is unblocked.
_comment_corridor_bands: VEG-CORRIDOR. The scatter's clumps/strays only ever sampled inside the old +-256m square (world_size below) -- everything past it, out to the corridor's real x+-1024/z-512..7680 (docs/decisions/D50/D51), was correctly-shaped baked ground with nothing growing on it. `density_scale` here (0..1, per band, TUNABLE) is the knob a content lane tunes to bring one band up as it gets authored -- NOT a single global figure, because a uniform full-density fill was measured to multiply the whole scatter's instance count and its ~45s share of boot by roughly the corridor:square area ratio (~64x), which is not affordable (see scatter_rules.gd::_place_corridor_fill's own header for the arithmetic). z ranges mirror terrain_playground.json's trail.bands (read, not imported -- this file owns scatter rules, not the spine) so a band's own reach matches the trail through it; z_max is exclusive, and the final band's max is the corridor's own z bound so nothing past band 5 is unaccounted for. A layer only fills the corridor at all if it opts in with its own `corridor_fill` key (see e.g. the `trees` layer below) -- absent is a no-op, same contract as verge/anchors.
_comment_visual_groundcover: VISUAL-GROUNDCOVER. ASSESSMENT_2026-08-23's blind critique ranked emptiness the #1 gap in every round -- '60-90% of most frames is one flat green terrain material with confetti scatter', named as the single biggest lever in the chapter. Every band was still floored at 0.03-0.07 against the origin square's own tuned 1.0, so a player spends nearly the whole 7.5km chapter on a fraction of the ground cover the opening square carries. Raised roughly 1.4-1.7x per band (not to parity -- see the header above for why a uniform full-density fill is not affordable) using headroom test_scatter_perf_budget.gd still had free (committed bake 143,630 vs its 260,000 sane ceiling): a config-fingerprint re-bake after this edit landed at 223,271, still under the ceiling (14% headroom left) but close enough that a further band-density bump belongs on a freshly-measured bake, not a guess from this one. Band 3 (the river lock, already the sparsest and shortest band) and band 5 (drain stations already thin the ground at run time) get the smallest bumps; band 4 (chapter's longest region, the one this lane's own band4 hero-tree work sits in) gets the largest, matching band4's own standing density request in DONE.md. TUNABLE.

trees._comment_harvest_r2_3: R2.3: the world's own scattered trees, not a second set of authored nodes on top of them -- makes the biggest single ground-cover layer double as the wood supply once harvest_node.gd's ~10 tutorial spots stop being enough. Originally 1-in-12 (0.083); HARVEST-ALL/D60 (owner directive) takes it to 1.0 -- every placed tree is harvestable, permanently, once chopped. trees._comment_leaf: R9.4. Leaves_NormalTree_C.png measures RGB(88,123,0) -- saturation 1.00, the maximum a colour can have, at hue 77, which is the same chartreuse the ground already is. The blind critic measured 91% of every saturated pixel in frames 01 and 04 inside one 30-degree hue bin and called the world monochromatic; the canopy was reinforcing the ground rather than contrasting with it. Leaves.png is the same pack's muted leaf -- RGB(114,131,50), saturation 0.62 -- and the retint warms it one step further off the grass hue. Same mechanism the bushes layer has used since the crimson-bush fix. No new asset. TUNABLE. R9.4 round 2: the retint now aims at palette.json's meadow.leaf_green_deep (#496c34, hue 98) rather than at a warm cream. Round 1 swapped the texture and stopped the canopy being the MOST saturated thing in frame, but left it at hue ~70 -- the same family as the ground, so frame_stats still measured 85-89% of chromatic pixels in one hue bin against the references' three to five. A canopy has to be a different green from the grass under it, not a brighter one.
trees._comment_leaf_magenta_fix: Backlog item 'A near-field tree renders with magenta/red-striped foliage', found in `dome-overview.png`/`road-end-lookup.png`. R9.4's own description of Leaves.png as a single 'muted leaf' colour was wrong: it is a MULTI-SPECIES SAMPLE SHEET -- green, blue, orange and a saturated magenta/pink leaf pair (measured RGB(216,55,135), full alpha) all on one 512x512 canvas. CommonTree's leaf cards are alpha-cutout billboards that each sample nearly the FULL 0-1 UV square (measured directly: median per-triangle UV bounding box 0.80x1.00 on CommonTree_1's canopy primitive), the same technique Leaves_NormalTree_C.png's own single-hue 'flower of leaflets' layout was built for. Pointed at Leaves.png instead, every card renders ALL of the atlas's leaf shapes at once, in their true colours -- confirmed with an isolated close-up repro (single tree, no terrain, no distance blending) that shows green, teal, orange AND magenta/crimson shards on one canopy. Reverted the swap target back to Leaves_NormalTree_C.png -- already proven safe as the `bushes` layer's own crimson-bush fix -- which removes the contamination entirely. Traded off: the round-2 desaturation this comment describes relied on Leaves.png's nonzero blue channel (texture*tint can only ever REDUCE saturation, never below what the base texture's own minimum channel allows, and Leaves_NormalTree_C.png's blue channel is 0 -- pinned at max saturation regardless of tint). The 3-step variant_retint hue spread below (94/97/81 degrees post-multiply) still applies and still gives CommonTree three distinguishable greens; only the saturation reduction R9.4 round 1 bought is given back. Not re-litigated here -- flagged honestly, not silently reintroduced.
trees._comment_variant: EV2: 'controlled material variants -- spring, deep and yellow-green -- not a different colour per tree' (bible sec10). Three fixed steps, one per remaining model, not per-instance jitter. Round 1 of EV2's own blind pass tried R9.4's shipped #9dcaff (`spring`) plus a straight darken (`deep`) -- both BLUE-hued multiplies (hue ~213) that land in the intended green family on Leaves.png's dark/average texels but multiply through nearly unchanged on bright highlight texels, reading as cyan/teal flecks a blind critic named directly. Round 2 fixed the hue (green-hued multiplies, hue 77-112, confirmed fleck-free by an independent second blind pass) but that pass's own close pixel inspection found the three still clustered in a 63-84 degree rendered hue band -- too narrow to read as distinguishable varieties once scene lighting compresses it further, even though the un-lit albedo maths looked separated. These values push both hue (77/96/103 after the same texture-multiply check) AND value (0.20/0.19/0.09) further apart -- `deep` in particular is now a genuinely darker tint, not just a different hue at the same brightness -- while the highlight-case check (a synthetic near-white texel) still stays inside 75-130 degrees, short of the ~150 degree line where the round-1 cyan artifact started.
trees._comment_bark_band2_floor: BAND2-FLOOR: the top-level `retint` above maps `Bark_NormalTree` to one colour (#b09985) for every model, so every CommonTree in the corridor shares one trunk tone regardless of which of the three canopy variants it is -- a blind critique of Band 2's forest floor named this directly, 'uniform salmon trunks'. `_tint_for` only falls back to the top-level map when a model's own `variant_retint` entry has no key for that material (vegetation.gd), so adding `Bark_NormalTree` here -- the canopy hue split already has three steps, the trunk had none -- is enough to give each of the three standard-canopy variants its own bark tone without a fourth model or a new texture: deep canopy gets darker bark, pale canopy gets lighter bark, the same direction the leaf split already goes. This is corridor-wide (variant_retint is keyed by model, not by band) because the uniform-trunk read is the same everywhere CommonTree grows and there is no per-band retint mechanism to narrow it to. Bark TEXTURE/material redesign -- the flat, undetailed bark surface itself -- is needs-art and not attempted here; recorded, not fixed.
trees._comment_anchors_of4_mound: OF4-remainder-mound. A BROKEN tree line along the rise's village-facing foot, and a few trees standing on the lower flank. A 7-9m tree is the cheapest ruler a landform can carry -- with nothing of known size anywhere on it the rise read as 'an enlarged pebble' to a blind critic, which is a scale failure, not a texture one. Slope is relaxed to 25 degrees for these draws only (this layer's own 21-degree ceiling stays as tuned everywhere else) so the line climbs a little way onto the flank instead of stopping dead at the break. Round 2: the three groups were the same size at the same radius and read as 'a ring following the hill's foot contour at near-even spacing' -- now one dense copse, one loose stand and one pair, at three different radii, which is the difference between a wood and a hedge. ALL TUNABLE.

south-west foot: just a pair, so the line is not continuous STRONGHOLD-R2: moved (70,-128) -> (60.5,-133.7). `paths.approaches`'s stronghold road contours the rise's south-west foot and passed 1.92m from the old centre, putting most of this anchor's own 9m disc inside the road's worn band -- measured, not assumed: with the road, seed 1 placed 0 of 2 and seed 99 placed 1 of 2; with the road stashed out, all three seeds the suite uses placed both (tools/_probe_anchor_seeds.gd, this task). BAND2-FLOOR round 2: a blind critique of this exact anchor's own frame (01-early-forest-day) still read the treeline as 'near-identical canopy size/height/tint... a scatter-brush pass'. Scale pushed further (1.4-1.75 -> 1.55-2.0, RNG-safe: a wider scale_min/scale_max range draws the same one randf_range() call per placed instance regardless of its bounds) so the two old trees are unmistakably a different age class. `count` deliberately left at 2, NOT raised -- `_place_anchor`'s attempt budget is `count * ANCHOR_ATTEMPTS_PER_INSTANCE`, drawn from this layer's single shared RNG stream (scatter_rules.gd::all_placements), and `_place_corridor_fill` runs after every anchor in that same stream for the WHOLE CORRIDOR, not just Band 2 -- raising `count` here was tried, rendered, and found to reshuffle corridor-wide tree corridor_fill enough that this exact frame's own midground/background treeline (the coverage that answers the region's core 'is there a forest here' complaint) thinned out, trading a solved complaint for a resurfaced one. Centred on the harvest.json order 2005/2006 cluster (135-145,1538-1543), the exact ground tools/survey_band2.gd's 01-early-forest-day frame looks at. This layer's own scale_min/max (0.55-1.35) already varies size but tops out short of an OLD tree beside young growth, which is the age-range read a closed canopy needs and the girth half of the same blind critique's complaint ('no leaf litter, undergrowth, fallen branches, saplings... uniform salmon trunks'). docs/reviews/band2/round-05 already measured that the corridor-wide trail-biased fill lands near none of Band 2's eight survey viewpoints by chance -- a density multiplier has nothing to multiply at a site it never reaches, so this is a hand-placed anchor, not a tuning number.

BAND2-FLOOR: same old-growth girth treatment as the early-forest anchor above, at the late-ridge site -- centred on harvest.json order 2004/2007 (68-76,2965-2972), the ground tools/survey_band2.gd's 05-late-ridge-day frame looks at.

A genuinely DIFFERENT species, not the same mesh retinted — which was the previous version of this layer and exactly what the critic caught. grove._comment_ev2: EV2 (bible sec10): 'hero trees' wants 2-3 large forms -- 'broad oak, asymmetrical old tree, tall landmark tree' -- not all 5. Measured with tools/measure_models.gd: TwistedTree_1 has the widest footprint (13.52x11.55, the 'broad oak'), TwistedTree_2 is the tallest (18.95m, the 'tall landmark tree'), and TwistedTree_4 is the only one of the five where depth exceeds width (10.38x11.29 -- a genuinely lopsided footprint, the 'asymmetrical old tree'). grove._comment_ev2_landmark_ceiling: EV2-landmark-ceiling: a blind critic ranked all 3 TwistedTree forms short of the key art's oaks -- 'canopies wider than they are tall, trunks visibly fork and lean' -- and TwistedTree_1 (the 'broad oak' slot, width/height 0.81) was the least-bad, still failing. grove._comment_count: Deliberately few. A 10,000-triangle tree is thirty times a Kenney one, and these are the biggest thing in the world — a stand of six is a landmark, forty is a forest nobody can walk through.

grove._comment_retexture: The pack ships `Leaves_TwistedTree_C` as a CRIMSON autumn leaf. Left alone it made the biggest trees in the meadow blood red and they dominated every frame. Warm hue has to come from the flowers, the dry grass and the golden hour, not from painting the whole canopy.
grove._comment_colour:
These stay CRIMSON, at the owner's call: 'I actually really like the red trees.'

grove._comment_leaf_magenta_fix: Magenta-canopy fix (see `trees` layer's own comment for the full mechanism): Leaves.png is a multi-species sample sheet, not a single muted leaf, and this layer's leaf cards sample nearly the whole canvas the same way CommonTree's do -- so the hero oaks carried the same green/blue/orange/magenta contamination. bushes._comment_harvest_fiber:
EXPEDITION-REST/REWARD-ECONOMY. Fiber had NO renewable source. Wood comes from the `trees` layer and stone from `rocks`, both at harvest_fraction 1.0 and both available anywhere the corridor has vegetation -- but fiber came only from five authored nodes in bands/band1_lower_meadows/harvest.json, all at z<=312, totalling 20, with no respawn anywhere in the system (D60 removed respawn outright). Against that: the recipes want 28 fiber (the Riding Saddle alone is 8, orb_prime 4, orb_greater 3) and the buildables want 22 more (camp 10, creature_bed 8, storage 4). 20 in the world against 50 asked for, all of it in the first 300m of a 7.5km chapter.
The consequence was prompt 61's whole premise: 'the player reaches a memorable buildable clearing with nearby basic resources ... place an injured creature in its physical bed'. Past Band 1 a player could not build a camp or a creature bed at any price, because the material did not exist to be gathered -- and a player who crafted the saddle and a Greater Orb on the critical path (13 fiber) could not afford one creature bed for the rest of the game.
Fixed on the mechanism that already ships, not a new one: `bushes` -- ferns and broad plants, the layer whose own comment calls it 'the middle layer' -- now yields fiber the same way trees yield wood. harvest_fraction 0.2 rather than trees' 1.0, using the lever _mark_harvestable's own comment describes as being there for exactly this ('a rare-resource species, say'): roughly one bush in five carries a prompt, so fiber is findable everywhere without adding a prompt to every shrub on the ROG's screen or doubling the world's harvest-point count. The stride is over draw order, not model, so the flowering bushes in this layer's model list carry it as often as the ferns do. ALL TUNABLE.

grass._comment_model_scale_world_grass: WORLD-GRASS. Per-model size, the lever scatter_rules.gd did not have until this lane added it (see its own note at the `model_scale` lookup). The layer's shared 0.26-0.58 range applies to all four species equally, so the 1.20m Wide_Short and the 1.84m Common_Tall could only ever differ by the 53% their raw meshes differ by -- and a blind critic looking at the result reported ONE asset: 'a single blade-fan type, always roughly knee height, always the same near-black green', and called the evenness generator output. Common_Tall's own top of range is the number to watch: 1.28m is above R9.4's rejected ~1.2m MEAN, but it is a maximum on one of four models rather than the layer's centre, and the layer's mean tuft is 0.60m. If a critic calls pampas again, this multiplier is the one to cut, not the shared range. TUNABLE. grass._comment_corridor_fill_vis_world: VIS-WORLD. `trail_bias` added -- this layer never had it. VEG-SITING gave trail_bias to trees/grove/saplings/deadfall/bushes and VISUAL-GROUNDCOVER gave it to path_stones, each time for the same measured reason (docs/reviews/band2/round-05: a uniform draw over a 2048m-wide box lands near none of the survey viewpoints, all of which stand ON the trail, so a density multiplier has nothing to multiply where the player actually is). The three layers that carpet the NEAR FIELD -- this one, drygrass and flowers -- were never revisited, so the primary ground cover was still drawn uniformly across 16.8 km2 while the player walks one line through it. That is why VISUAL-GROUNDCOVER's chapter-wide bump (143,630 -> 223,889 placements) measured only ~4% mean improvement: it multiplied a distribution that mostly misses the camera. This adds NO instances -- `density_scale` stays 1.0 -- it only moves where the existing candidates' clump centres land. Arithmetic for band 3 (the thinnest, density_scale 0.05) before this change: ~68 kept clumps of radius 10m over 3.24 km2, so ~0.66% of the band's ground carried a grass clump at all, and stray grass ran one tuft per ~5,800 m2. 0.65 rather than the 0.85 the tree layers use: a carpet layer concentrated as hard as a copse layer stops being a meadow and becomes a green ribbon down a bald plain, so a third of the fill deliberately stays wherever the unbiased box draw puts it. `trail_offset_min` 0 lets clump edges reach the worn dirt; `path_standoff` (0.3-7m, ~17m wavelength, per side) is what culls them there, which is the mechanism OF12 built for a raveled edge and which until now had almost no cover to ravel. TUNABLE.

corridor_fill._comment_density_scale_ground_layers: GROUND-LAYERS. Deliberately DOWN, reversing this lane's own rounds 2-3. Those rounds answered 'the ground reads as one flat material' with scatter density and took the chapter from 143,630 to 532,886 placements for no measured change in the blind near-field clump count. The reason is in ralph/reports/VISUAL_WORLD_SURFACE_2026-08-23.md and it is geometric: the near field is terrain SURFACE, not somewhere a mesh can stand, so the ground's appearance is a material problem and scatter was the wrong instrument for it. With the terrain now carrying real material variation (terrain_playground.json `macro`, the drygrass and damp layers), scatter goes back to what it is good at: accent and silhouette break-up, over open readable ground. The target composition is roughly 70% open grass, 15% path/worn, 10% low accents, 5% special patches -- so the meadow needs NEGATIVE SPACE, which density was actively destroying. The siting (trail_bias) and the clustering (clump_radius, the strays/per_clump ratio) are KEPT: they cost nothing and they are what make the accents land where the player walks and read as drifts rather than sprinkle. TUNABLE, and the honest first thing to give back if the ROG Ally needs headroom.

grass._comment_colour_jitter_vis_world: VIS-WORLD. REMOVED, and the reason is a confirmed bug rather than a taste call. `colour_jitter > 0` is the only thing that sets `needs_instance_colour`, and vegetation.gd::_tint_for then forces `vertex_color_use_as_albedo` ON. This pack's meshes carry a COLOR_0 vertex attribute that is a baked ambient-occlusion gradient -- decoding Grass_Common_Tall.gltf's own accessor measures mean vertex colour 0.001 at the lowest 15% of vertices against 0.962 at the highest -- and albedo_color MULTIPLIES, so forcing it into albedo rendered the bottom third of every blade solid black. That is the defect reported as 'grass tufts render BLACK on back faces'; it is NOT a culling bug (every source declares doubleSided and the imported material reads cull_mode=2, CULL_DISABLED, verified by probe). The imported material's own `vertex_color_use_as_albedo` is FALSE, also verified by probe, so removing the jitter lets it fall back to off and the blade renders its texture. The channel cannot be split: Godot routes MultiMesh per-instance colour through the same switch, so keeping the jitter and disabling the vertex colour would silently kill the jitter instead. Colour variety is recovered below by `variant_retint`, which is per-MODEL and needs no vertex colour at all. Stripping COLOR_0 by rebuilding the surface was considered and rejected: _retint's own comment records that surface_get_arrays()/add_surface_from_arrays() silently drops the importer's generated LOD chain and shadow mesh, a regression this repo has already paid for once.

flowers._comment: Colour accents, clustered hard. Wildflowers grow in patches; spread evenly they read as confetti. Clover is in here because a flower patch with nothing between the blooms reads as pins in a board.
flowers._comment_density: The critic measured saturated non-green pixels below the horizon at 0.000%-0.035% of frame against a design brief that says 'wildflower meadows', and found ZERO in one frame out of 921,600 pixels. A colour accent nobody can see is not an accent.
flowers._comment_models_world_grass: WORLD-GRASS: Clover_1/Clover_2 move OUT, to the new `groundmat` layer below. They were here because, in this layer's own words, 'a flower patch with nothing between the blooms reads as pins in a board' -- correct diagnosis, wrong layer. Clover is foliage, not bloom, and sharing the flower layer forced it to share the flower SCALE: VISUAL-GROUNDCOVER's measured 0.025-0.09 is right for a blossom head and puts a clover clump at 3-11cm, which is under the terrain's own texture frequency and therefore invisible. Split out, each layer gets the scale its own job needs, and this one becomes purely floral -- which is what lets the drifts below read as flower drifts.
flowers._comment_retint_ground_layers: GROUND-LAYERS. This was the only ground-cover layer with NO retint, which means vegetation.gd left albedo_color pure white and the layer rendered its source textures unmodified at full brightness. A blind critic read the result exactly: the pond-side sprites 'render full-bright and read as floating confetti or UI markers, not plants', and the stream agave is 'lit like an item pickup'. Checked before assuming: all 46 gltf files in stylized_nature carry ZERO emission, so this is albedo, not an emissive material like the one the character rigs turned out to have. Multiplying the petals toward the key art's own muted lilac and the foliage toward the meadow olive puts them in the same light as everything around them. Petals stay the lightest ground cover in the set on purpose -- they are the accent the composition budget reserves 5% for. TUNABLE.
flowers._comment_drift_world_grass: WORLD-GRASS: tighter, fewer, bigger drifts. clump_radius 9.0 -> 6.0, per_clump 78 -> 120, strays 620 -> 320 -- a net ~50 fewer placements, redistributed. Same trade R7.1-remainder and VIS-WORLD both made for the grass layer and for the same measured reason: uniform singles read as confetti and clusters read as placed. Prompt 72 asks for this by name off the reference ('the reference's pink drifts are tight and irregular'), and moong-02/03 show why -- their flower patches are dense enough to read as one pink shape at fifty metres, which no evenly-spread sprinkle at any count does. 120 in a 113 m2 disc is ~1.06/m2 inside a drift against 0.31 before. TUNABLE.
flowers._comment_corridor_fill: VEG-CORRIDOR: colour accents fill at the band table's own rate, same as the other ground cover.

corridor_fill._comment_density_scale_b11: B11 ground-cover density. 1.0 -> 1.5. flowers._comment_path_of12: OF12: this layer's whole path-anchoring stack -- path_bias 0.35, path_bias_per_clump 26, path_bias_side_offset 6.0, path_bias_jitter 4.0, grown one knob per round across EV3-remainder through -4 (the full history is in DONE.md, kept there rather than here) -- is REMOVED, not retuned. Wildflowers are now ordinary meadow accents that reach a path only when an unbiased clump happens to land near one, gated by the same noise-varying path_standoff as grass (scatter_rules.gd::path_standoff_at) so a chance near-path clump keeps a ragged, per-side-independent edge instead of a matched pair of crescents. max is lower than grass's -- verge wildflowers genuinely hug a worn edge -- and the salt differs so flower gaps do not mirror grass gaps. TUNABLE.

This is deliberately NOT the chapter-wide density lever VISUAL-GROUNDCOVER already pushed for ~4% mean gain; the broad trailside cover comes from `corridor_fill.trail_bias` above at no instance cost, and this only thickens the metre or two either side of the dirt that the standoff noise ravels. verge._comment_vis_world_r3: VIS-WORLD round 3: see grass's matching entry. Moved out with grass so the ground thins ONCE, gradually, rather than in steps. No placements added -- this is a render-side number and the placements are byte-identical for it. The key art's flowers are an ankle-height carpet. Cut to a quarter, which puts heads at ankle-to-shin. TUNABLE -- but check any change against a person in frame, not by eye.

DEEPER than the waterline on purpose: a boulder breaking the surface near the shore is one of the contact points the water's foam band exists for. TUNABLE.
rocks._comment_min_height_op21_19: OP21-19 raised all ten layer floors by +5.5m to stop trees and bushes standing in the relocated pond, and the accompanying scatter_rules.gd change added a hard water_level()-0.5 floor as a GATE inside _consider. Both are REVERTED here and replaced by scatter_rules.gd::_drop_below_waterline, a filter over the finished list. The gate was the bug: _thin_by_drain's own header already states the rule it broke -- a rejection inside _consider happens BEFORE an instance's scale, model and yaw are drawn, so every later instance in that layer lands on different random numbers. The pond is ~0.02% of a 8192x2048m corridor and the re-roll was total: 257 region files changed, and it stood a rock and a pebble on a slope in the practice meadow at (59.7, -49.1) where smoke_traversal.gd's OF15 detector caught a held move_back dead-stopped for a full second. These per-layer floors are back at the values main shipped, because with the filter in place the raise bought nothing: the filter is stricter than any of them at the pond and touches nothing anywhere else. rocks._comment_align: R9.4-remainder-8-followup: a rock deliberately biased toward slopes but placed world-up, sampled at one centre point, hangs over the downhill side of its own footprint with a visible gap under it -- confirmed in a render, a boulder perched on the hillside behind the farmhouse with daylight showing under its downhill edge. Rocks are rigid, so they should rest flush with the slope; unlike grass/bushes/trees, which stay world-up on purpose (a plant grows against gravity, not perpendicular to the ground it's rooted in).
rocks._comment_harvest_r2_3: R2.3: the world's own scattered rocks, the stone-gathering half of the same fix trees got above. Originally 1-in-14 (0.071); HARVEST-ALL/D60 (owner directive) takes it to 1.0, same as trees -- every placed rock is harvestable, permanently.
rocks._comment_tint_r9_4: R9.4. Same treatment, milder, for the same reason: Rocks_Diffuse's faces measure value 0.46 at saturation 0.09, which is a cool light grey sitting on warm ground. The blind critic also noted the rock field is 'one prop instanced rather than a rock field' -- that part is scale_min/scale_max below, not colour. TUNABLE.
rocks._comment_variant_r9_4_remainder_8:
R9.4-remainder-8-rocks-repeat: a blind critic named the rock clusters 'one rock instance duplicated, not a quarry of varied stone' -- same shape, same size, SAME COLOUR, evenly spaced. scale_min/scale_max already vary size (0.28-2.1) and the layer only has 3 boulder meshes to draw from (the fuller Stylized Nature MegaKit that might carry more rock forms is itch.io-blocked, EV1-remainder), so the one remaining honest lever is colour, the same one EV2 used to split one tree mesh into spring/deep/yellow-green variants.
Round 1: three hue-only variants in one narrow value band -- crushed by scene shading, a fresh critic still saw 'no colour/tone variation'.
Round 2: kept hue close but spread VALUE hard (a near-black variant, a near-white one). Real, measured pixel movement, but a fresh critic's own read was sharper than a pass/fail: 'the tonal difference... is lit-face vs shadow-face on the SAME mesh, not a material variant -- rotate the camera and the different rock would go dark too... no true colour/material variety, only lighting-driven contrast.' A pure value swing is genuinely ambiguous with directional-light shading on a faceted low-poly mesh, which already produces its own strong per-face brightness range -- exactly the confound the critic named.
Round 3 changes the axis that lighting can't fake: HUE. A single white directional light changes a Lambertian surface's VALUE with face angle but not its hue, so three genuinely different hue families (warm tan, cool blue-grey slate, rust-brown ironstone) read as different minerals regardless of which face catches the sun -- unlike round 2's same-hue-different-value pair, which a shaded face and a lit face of one rock can produce by themselves. TUNABLE.
rocks._comment_colour_jitter_r9_4_remainder_8: Same mechanism R7.1-remainder used for grass -- per-instance MultiMesh colour multiplier, zero extra draw calls or geometry (vegetation.gd). Pulled back from round 2's 0.22: a wide VALUE-only jitter reinforces exactly the lighting-looking-like-variety confound round 2's critic named, so this now does modest per-instance value spread on top of the three real hue families above rather than trying to carry the whole effect itself. Applies to the pebble meshes too (material PathRocks, untouched by variant_retint above), a second, cheaper source of per-instance variety in the same clump.
rocks._comment_scale_r9_4: R9.4. Was 0.35-1.3, a 3.7x span that still read as one size because most draws land near the middle. Widened to 0.28-2.1 so a clump has boulders AND pebbles in it. TUNABLE.
rocks._comment_anchors_of4_mound: OF4-remainder-mound. Authored outcrops and a talus apron on the ONLY faces of `rises.peaks[0]` the village square and the Rise road can see (the arc from the north-west limb round to the south-west, computed from the two vantage eyes with `tools/_probe_mound.gd`, not guessed). A whole-map placement dump found FOUR rock instances in that entire wedge and none of them on the landform: this layer's own 44-degree ceiling excludes most of a 46m rise's flank, so the layer whose stated job is to make steep ground read as stone was locked out of the steepest ground in the game, and a blind critic read the hill as 'an enlarged pebble' with 'nothing on it, in it, or at the top of it'. Each anchor raises `max_slope_deg` FOR ITS OWN DRAWS ONLY (scatter_rules.gd::_place_anchor) -- the meadow scatter's ceiling is unchanged, so this cannot put boulders on cliffs anywhere else. The `west-spur` pair also absorbs the lone boulder at (80.3,-63.9) that two blind critics independently called 'a stray blob / floating chunk': it is still there, now with company. ALL TUNABLE.
rocks._comment_anchors_of4_mound_r2: Round 2 restructure, and the reason the anchors come in PAIRS. Round 1 gave each site 7-9 boulders in one 1.4-3.2 scale band, and the blind critic's worst-scale-offender finding was the fix itself: 'roughly twenty-five to thirty of them on one hillside... they shrink the hill -- a landform you can count off in five or six boulder-widths from foot to crest is not a landmark... and they are all the same size. No cobbles, no gravel, no single house-sized monolith.' A rock that is a scale REFERENCE has to be either much bigger or much smaller than the thing beside it; a field of same-sized blocks is a ruler with one mark on it. So every site is now a `-block` anchor (one or two large stones) plus a `-rubble` anchor at the same centre and a wider radius (ten-odd cobbles), the big stones weighted toward the FOOT where gravity actually leaves them rather than spread evenly up the face, and `sink` buries a fraction of each so they sit in the ground instead of resting tangent on it. Large stones (scale >= 1.9) went from ~40 to 11.

path_stones._comment_paths: The one layer allowed on the dirt paths: stones on a path ARE the path.
path_stones._comment_path_bias_ev3: EV3, found while blind-judging EV4's paths: this layer predated the real paths and its clumps were never anchored to them, so a stone cluster could land several metres of untouched lawn away from the nearest route -- 'a tidy circular stone group... disconnected from the actual path' per the blind critic. path_bias 1.0 snaps every clump centre to the nearest point on `paths.routes` (scatter_rules.gd::_clump_centre); the clump's own clump_radius then spreads instances off that point, so a cluster straddles the road and reads as stones trodden into it rather than scattered independently of it. strays (90) are left unbiased on purpose -- they are the loose stones elsewhere in the meadow, not the path's own texture.
path_stones._comment_clump_radius_ev3_remainder_5: EV3-remainder-5: clump_radius was 8.0, more than twice the path's own visible width (terrain_playground.json paths.width 3.0 + shoulder 1.5 = 4.5m total fade band). A whole-map dump of grandpas-house-route.png's actual region -- the one specific frame two blind critics kept calling a hedge after every ground-cover mechanism (flowers/bushes/grass/drygrass) had already been ruled out by real placement data -- found this layer is the ONLY thing besides grass/flowers there, and split almost perfectly symmetric (7 left / 7 right / 4 on-path of 18 in-frame instances, individual stones up to 7-8m off the path centreline). That is exactly the 'matched clusters... flanking both sides' shape the critics described, on a layer nobody had checked yet. 3.5m keeps the spread inside roughly the path-plus-shoulder-plus-a-verge band instead of forming two crescents on open lawn well past where the path itself has any visual influence.
path_stones._comment_tint_r9_4: R9.4. PathRocks_Diffuse.png is an atlas of pale lavender-grey stones on a dark green ground -- the stone faces measure RGB(132,135,130), value 0.53, saturation 0.04, i.e. a neutral light grey. Rendered over a bright meadow under a strong sun they blew out to RGB(229,230,231) and read, in the survey frames, as scattered paper or marble chips rather than as stones trodden into a path. This is not a bug -- the texture is being drawn faithfully -- it is the wrong value for earth. Warmed and darkened to about the value of the soil they sit in. TUNABLE.
path_stones._comment_align_t1_ground: T1-GROUND, 2026-08-30, item 3 (floating path pebbles). These are RIGID flat plates -- 1.06-2.13m across, 0.11m thick (ralph/DONE.md's own RockPath measurement) -- and this layer allows up to 14 degrees of slope with only a single centre-point height sample, exactly the shape of defect `rocks`' own `_comment_align` already fixed: a wide rigid prop sampled at one point hangs over the downhill side with daylight showing under it. At 14 degrees a 2m-wide plate has ~0.5m of vertical mismatch across its own footprint -- read in a blind pass as 'the pebbles hover a few cm above the dirt... reading as scattered rather than embedded'. Same fix, same mechanism (scatter_rules.gd already supports this per-layer, opt-in, exactly because plants must NOT get it): rest flush with the slope instead of standing world-up on it, plus a shallow sink to bury the rim `align_to_slope` alone still leaves showing on broken ground. No re-bake needed for the align itself (scatter_rules.gd reads it at placement time), but this layer's own values feed the scatter bake, so a bake IS required after this edit. TUNABLE.

groundmat._comment: WORLD-GRASS. THE TIER BETWEEN THE GROUND AND THE TUFTS, and the answer to the defect a blind critic ranked second in this lane's round-1 pass: 'each grass tuft meets the ground at a razor line with no skirt, no thinning, no smaller filler geometry -- props stabbed into dirt'. The same critic assumed the fix needed art that is not in the build. It does not: Clover_1/Clover_2 were already vendored and already placed, just at flower scale (3-11cm) where nothing could see them, and Plant_1_Big was vendored and referenced by NOTHING. This layer is those three at sizes that do a job, and it adds no asset to the repository. LAST IN THE LAYER ORDER ON PURPOSE, and this is not cosmetic: scatter_rules.gd::all_placements seeds each layer as base_seed + INDEX * 7919, so a new layer inserted anywhere but the end re-seeds every layer after it. Measured when this one was first written between `flowers` and `rocks`: the rocks layer moved 5,697 -> 5,669 placements and path_stones 9,243 -> 9,420 for no edit of their own, which is the same class of silent reshuffle STRONGHOLD-R2 chased when the road cairn's anchor started placing 0 of 3 on some seeds. Append new layers here; do not insert them.
groundmat._comment_models: Three models, three jobs, separated by `model_scale` rather than by three layers -- one layer means one Terrain3DMeshAsset registration per model and one shared RNG stream, three would mean three of each. NOTE the hard constraint that decided which models could be used at all: vegetation.gd::_layer_for resolves a model to the FIRST layer whose `models` list holds it, and _build_batch groups by model, so a mesh listed in two layers silently renders both layers' placements with one layer's retint, LOD, shadow and collision settings (vegetation.json's own `_comment_ev2` records the same trap for the rock meshes). So Clover had to LEAVE the flowers layer to arrive here, and Plant_7/Plant_7_Big -- the obvious mat candidates at 0.25m tall -- could not be used at all, because they belong to `bushes` and Band 2's authored understorey anchors depend on them there.
groundmat._comment_model_scale: Raw mesh heights are Clover_1 1.14m, Clover_2 1.26m, Plant_1_Big 3.76m, so the shared 0.24-0.46 range lands them at: clover 0.27-0.58m, the low leafy mat that skirts a grass tuft's base and breaks the hard line where it meets the terrain; Plant_1_Big at 0.44 -> 0.40-0.76m and ~0.31-0.59m across, a broadleaf standing above the mat and below the tufts. That is the ground->mid->canopy ladder prompt 72 asks for in its item 3, built from what is already here.
groundmat._comment_density: Sized against the placement ceiling, not by feel. The committed bake before this layer is 561,891 against test_scatter_perf_budget.gd's 900,000, so this layer's budget is what fits inside that gap with headroom left for the next lane. Clumped hard (per_clump 150 in a 5.5m radius is ~1.6/m2 inside a drift) and trail-sited at the grass layer's own bias, because the arithmetic that governs every ground layer here is that a uniform fill over 16.8 km2 of corridor is unaffordable at any density that would be visible -- see ralph/reports/WORLD_GRASS_2026-08-25.md. The verge is where this tier earns most: it is the metre or two either side of the worn dirt, which is the ground a player looks at more than any other in the chapter. TUNABLE, and this whole layer is the cheapest thing to cut if the Ally needs headroom -- it is the smallest geometry in the world and the least missed at distance.
groundmat._comment_retint: Deliberately DARKER and less saturated than the grass tufts above. This tier is the one that reads as shadow under the taller growth, and the same blind critic's separate finding is that this build has 'no quarter-tone anywhere' -- bimodal blown sand against crushed black. A mat sitting a little under the tuft's own value is where a quarter-tone comes from. Two greens rather than one so the two clovers are not one repeated sprite, the same treatment `grass` and `drygrass` already carry. TUNABLE, and re-derive against the tufts rather than by eye.
groundmat._comment_lod: Short on purpose, and shorter than every layer above it. These are the smallest meshes in the scatter; past ~70m a 0.3m clover is sub-pixel and costs a draw to render nothing. The fade band is wide relative to the range for the same reason grass's is -- a hard cutoff on the densest layer is the bald ring this lane exists to remove, and it must not be reintroduced by the layer that fixes it. TUNABLE, and the first ground layer to give back if the Ally needs GPU headroom.

_comment_retint: Mostly EMPTY now, and that is the point. The Kenney kit shipped a bright teal-green palette that had to be remapped wholesale; this pack ships real textures, and `albedo_color` multiplies them, so an unmapped material passes through as authored. Only the deliberate per-layer modulates above apply. A strong colour here would come out as shadow, not as hue.
_comment_retint_bark_ev2: EV2-trunk-colour. Root cause found by rendering the SAME trunk close-up (full texel resolution, no minification) and comparing to the unlit source texture: Bark_NormalTree measures RGB(140,88,67) in the file but rendered at RGB(~217,167,134) in-scene, and Bark_TwistedTree measures RGB(84,76,72) but rendered at RGB(~167,162,153) -- both washed toward the SAME neutral cool tone, and disabling art.json's ambient_light_energy (0 -> still washed toward warm-boosted brown but no longer pale/pink) confirmed ambient_colour (#a8bccc, a cool blue-grey deliberately tuned for GROUND shadow legibility by an earlier fix) is the dominant contributor -- not distance/minification, the item's original guess. Thin curved trunk geometry has proportionally more of its surface at grazing angles to the sun than a flat ground plane, so it draws a larger share of its total light from that cool ambient fill, which a global ambient recolour would fix for bark at the cost of re-breaking the ground legibility fix it exists for. Same lever as the `rocks` layer's own `_comment_tint_r9_4` fix for the identical class of problem (a warm/neutral source washed cool by scene lighting): retint the texture warmer/darker so the SAME lighting pipeline lands on a believable bark colour instead of correcting the light itself. Values solved from the measured gain (rendered/source, per channel) against a target of ~RGB(150,100,70) for normal bark and ~RGB(95,82,72) for the already-greyer twisted bark; verified by re-rendering the same close-up framing after applying.
_comment_collision: Layers marked `collides` get real static collision. Two reasons, and the second is the urgent one: a tree you can walk through reads as a hologram, and — because the camera's SpringArm3D only stops at things with collision — a bush with none lets the camera end up INSIDE it. Two survey frames came back showing nothing but green because the camera was inside a bush during a fight. Grass and flowers must never collide; you walk through those.
_comment_clearings: BAND-SPLIT-2. `clearings` and `footprints` used to live here, both positional and both monolithic near the origin, which meant a band author who could add a creature, a prop, a harvest node or a trainer still could not add a clearing around their own structure without editing this shared file. They are now cut per corridor band, under data/config/bands/<band>/vegetation.json, and merged back at load by scripts/data/band_content.gd -- same treatment BAND-SPLIT gave spawns/props/harvest/trainers. Every entry carries an `order`; the merge sorts by it, so the merged arrays are identical to the pre-split file (tests/test_band_vegetation.gd pins that against tests/fixtures/band_split_baseline/vegetation.json). The scatter *rules* below (layers, corridor_bands, retint) are unrelated and stayed put -- see D54's own 'vegetation is deliberately not split' note, which was true for rules and was never about these two positional arrays.
_comment_footprints: See `_comment_clearings` above -- footprints moved the same way, for the same reason.
_comment_lod: PERF-2: each layer's lod_range/lod_fade_margin set Terrain3DMeshAsset's lod0_range/fade_margin (vegetation.gd::_make_mesh_asset) -- the view-distance beyond which that layer's instances stop rendering, and the width of the fade band leading up to it. Bigger/more important props (trees, rocks) get a longer range than tiny ground cover (grass, flowers) so the world does not visibly thin at ordinary play distances while the cheapest, least-visible-at-range layers stop costing draw calls first. TUNABLE -- render before/after and run visual-judge before changing.
